 Trenton mayoral runoff election awaits legal decision about early voting

 Corey Isiah McNair, left, and W. Reed Gusciora speak at the Trentonian and Trenton Journal’s mayoral forum hosted by Mercer County Community College in September.
(File photos by John Berry/ The Trentonian)
 By L.A. Parker | laparker@trentonian.com | The Trentonian PUBLISHED: November 10, 2026 at 4:49 PM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... LAWRENCE — A Mercer County Board of Elections committee said members await word from state attorneys regarding procedures for the City of Trenton mayoral runoff.
 Being discussed is whether city residents will have a three-day opportunity to vote early before the scheduled Dec. 8 runoff date between Corey McNair and two-term incumbent Mayor Reed Gusciora. McNair, a Trenton police officer finished almost 1,700 votes ahead of Gusciora. An initial report expected early voting from Dec.4-6.
 “It’s not our decision,” said Jill Moyer, chairperson for the Board of Elections. Secretary Martin Jennings, Jr. chorused the response from a board that includes Commissioners Mary Corrigan and Gino Melone.
 Both Trenton mayoral candidates support early voting.
 “Absolutely,” said Gusciora, who pressed for at least one debate with McNair before runoff voting begins. The McNair camp released a statement saying that residents heard from candidates from August through October. McNair respectfully declined.
 McNair attended the Mercer County Board of Elections meeting and explained his support for early voting. He said voters should have opportunities to cast ballots over several days instead of one day.
 In fact, McNair posted an online video informing people they had options for casting runoff election votes. Mercer County Board of Elections expect a decision soon.
 Mercer County Clerk Paula Sollami Covello said city residents will have access to mail-in voting.
